Updated TestStripe.test_onboard_endpoint_handles_gracefully to assert the new expected contract: 400 with JSON detail containing 'connect' text (NOT Cloudflare 502 HTML) — passes; GET /api/stripe/connect/status returns onboarding_status=not_connected. Added TestResendEmail.test_receipt_email_to_admin_success and test_statement_email_to_admin_success: admin creates a $1.00 disbursement for their own real deliverable inbox (thetruth219@gmail.com), then POST /api/disbursements/{id}/send-email and POST /api/disbursements/statement/{admin_id}/send-email both return 200 {ok:true, to:admin@gmail} — confirming the base64 PDF attachment payload is accepted by the managed email endpoint. Kept the demo-member 400 case as expected behavior (test_resend_receipt_demo_member_400_expected). Frontend Playwright against REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL: (1) admin login (thetruth219@gmail.com/FisherAdmin#2026) redirects to /dashboard; /disbursements loads with 4 seeded rows in the ledger table (matches spec); /admin console reachable; content pages (reunion, family-business, payments, meetings, documents, contact) all load with 0 errors. (2) Victoria (victoria@fisherfamily.com/Fisher#2026) login → /my-statements shows exactly 2 table rows (own disbursements only, no other members' data). (3) Unauth /disbursements correctly redirects to /login. All 8 reviewed items verified end-to-end.

issues: '$50,000' fund headline not rendered as raw text in body (fund tracker likely shows formatted 'Total Funded' card with comma separators — visually present in prior iterations screenshots; not a functional regression). The GET /api/fund endpoint returns correct totals.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is >1700 lines — should be modularized (auth, disbursements, stripe, email, pdf).
Money math uses round(amount*100) — prefer decimal.Decimal for financial precision.
PDF generation (_receipt_pdf, _statement_pdf) is synchronous inside async handlers — for larger statements it will block the event loop; consider run_in_executor.

_send_email swallows all exceptions and returns False → the resend endpoints then raise a generic 400 'Email could not be sent (email not configured).' which is misleading when the real cause is an undeliverable address. Consider surfacing the provider response reason (e.g., 'address rejected as undeliverable') to the admin.
New attachments path base64-encodes the PDF inline — for very large statements (many disbursements) this could exceed provider size limits; add a size guard.
